questions.question: What is an outcome in a sample space $S$?
options: A subset of $S$ that contains many results
The probability assigned to the whole sample space
A numerical summary of repeated experiments
An element $\omega\in S$ representing one possible result

questions.question: Which notation expresses that $\omega$ is an outcome in the sample space $S$?
options: $S\in\omega$
$\omega\subseteq S$
$\omega\in S$
$P(\omega)=S$

questions.question: How detailed is an outcome?
options: It is always only a yes-or-no answer, in all instances without exception.
It is the most detailed result considered by the chosen model
It must always be a real number
It is less detailed than every event

questions.question: How are events related to outcomes?
options: Outcomes are collections of events
Events are collections of outcomes
Events cannot contain outcomes
Every outcome must contain the whole sample space

questions.question: What determines the level of detail in an outcome?
options: How the experiment is modeled
The largest probability in the model
The number of events already named
Whether the outcome is written in Greek letters

questions.question: For one die roll modeled by the face shown, which is an outcome?
For two coin tosses modeled as ordered pairs, which is a single outcome?
If $S=\{a,b,c\}$, which expression names an outcome?
options: $\emptyset$

questions.question: In a customer-order model, which record is best interpreted as one outcome?
options: the set of every possible order record
(purchase amount, item type, delivery time)
the event that delivery is late
the probability of buying an item

questions.question: If the realized outcome is $\omega=3$ in $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$, which event occurs?
options: $\emptyset$

questions.question: Why is $\{2,4,6\}$ usually not a single outcome for one die roll modeled by face?
options: It is the complement of a single face, but that is not the issue
It is outside the sample space $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$
It records too much detail for a die roll
It is a set of several faces, not one element of $S$

questions.question: If a model records only whether a die roll is even or odd, what can be an outcome?
options: the exact face $4$ as a required distinction
even
the event 'roll at least five'

questions.question: Which distinction is correct?
options: An outcome is always a set; an event is always a number
An outcome is one possible result; an event is a set of possible results
An outcome is assigned probability one; an event is assigned probability zero
An outcome must be continuous; an event must be discrete

questions.question: Let $S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$. Which option is an event rather than a single outcome?
options: $HH$
$TT$
$TH$

questions.question: A two-coin model records only the number of heads. Which is a possible outcome?
options: $HH$

questions.question: For $S=[0,+\infty)$ in a waiting-time model, which is a single outcome?
Why might $(H,T)$ and the number $1$ both be defensible outcomes for two coin tosses in different models?
options: They must be the same outcome in every sample space
One is valid only if probabilities are not assigned
The number $1$ cannot be an outcome because it is numerical
They correspond to different choices of recorded detail

questions.question: A sample space $S$ collects every possible result of a random experiment. Which object is a single outcome?
options: It is any subset that has positive probability
It is the same object as the probability function
It is one element selected from the modeled sample space
It is always the event that actually has probability one

questions.question: In $S=\{(i,j):i,j\in\{1,\ldots,6\}\}$ for two ordered dice, which is a single outcome?
Suppose $S$ records full customer orders as triples $(amount,type,time)$. Which statement is most accurate?
options: all late orders must be one outcome, while a triple is an event
$(25,\text{book},2)$ can be an outcome, while all late orders form an event
the sample space must be only the set of delivery times
a customer-order model cannot have structured outcomes
